subject.title: [Bug]: Dreaming deep promotion biased to stale 3-5 day old content; REM produces repetitive meta-themes; promotion gates bypassed via phase-signal boost

question: For memory-core deep promotion, which evidence types should satisfy default promotion gates: organic recall only, explicitly grounded durable evidence, daily/session repeated signals, or separate thresholds for each?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally allow daily-only and grounded-only evidence to pass default gates, while multiple production reports show zero-recall daily/session artifacts polluting durable memory; automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Split gate evidence from scoring evidence
options.body: Require organic recall or explicitly grounded durable evidence to satisfy promotion gates, keep daily/session signals as ranking context, and update rank/apply/docs/tests together.

options.title: Preserve aggregate daily/session gates
options.body: Keep daily/session signals eligible for promotion gates and focus only on denoising, recency, placeholder filtering, and diagnostics for noisy workspaces.

options.title: Decompose into narrower canonical items
options.body: Track aggregate signal gating, query/day diversity, light ordering, and REM placeholder behavior separately, then close this umbrella only after those decisions land.

recommendation.title: Split gate evidence from scoring evidence
recommendation.body: Require organic recall or explicitly grounded durable evidence to satisfy promotion gates, keep daily/session signals as ranking context, and update rank/apply/docs/tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal because their history includes the daily-only promotion behavior and repeated recent work across the affected memory-core promotion surface.
